differences.comparison: Omit message IDs before normalizing generated task UUIDs; compare all other projected message fields, mode order, paths and output.
differences.reason: The text-only bridge carries content and usage, not provider message IDs. Python LangChain generates fresh IDs.
The JavaScript provider boundary returns fixed content-free errors rather than framework or host exception text.
The adapter maps native recursion exhaustion to the framework-neutral budget error after the same 25-step stream.

limits: LangGraph Python tool-call replies spike: binding/replies, streaming, confirmed writes, safety floor and durable replay have text-protocol alternatives; native tool binding and neighbouring tool/message shapes remain refused. The test-local helper failed swallowed-terminal-code containment and no production source shipped.

Tool-reply alternatives compare final text, ordered host calls and write count on CPython and Node Pyodide, including checked JSON text, host approval/decline, budget termination, private-result destination refusal and one write across fresh-Worker restore/replay. They supply no ToolNode, schema-constrained choice or streamed tool deltas; direct capability calls omit the helper tool-policy flag.

New tool-reply probes have no Chromium reload, Firefox, WebKit or real-model measurement. Existing twelve-case projections, case names, golden bytes and locks are unchanged. Inherited Python bind_tools raises NotImplementedError rather than GalaxieError; fixed Worker translation depends on boot versus run.
Pyodide lanes compare projected stream events for eight cases, and pending values and final counters for the four original interrupt cases; complete checkpoint histories are native-only.
Interrupt-subgraph reload compares the same pending ID/value and final counters after reconstruction; accepted-answer reconciliation is covered by the three original reload cases.
Models and capability replies are deterministic fixtures. No real model or external network is used.
